柱.meaning: A pompous <part>lord</part> brags that his new banquet hall rests on solid gold. During the feast the roof creaks, and the guests see that the only thing holding it up is one living <part>tree</part> growing through the floor, its branches spread under the ceiling. The lord hangs his crown on it and calls it his finest <kanji>pillar</kanji>.
柱.on: A squirrel on the trunk stuffs <sound>chew</sound>ing gum into every crack to keep it steady.
柱.kun: A <sound>ha</sound>rp plays, a <sound>shee</sound>p dances, and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men is set down at the tree's roots.

揚.meaning: A tiny fishing boat is stuck: its rusty <part>anchor</part> won't come up. The captain ties the chain to the morning <part>sunbeams</part>, and as the sun climbs, the anchor rises with it, dripping seaweed. She sips her tea and lets the sun do the work to <kanji>hoist</kanji> it.
揚.on: Once it's up, the anchor bobs on its chain like a giant <sound>yo</sound>-yo.
揚.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps the crew, as the anchor swings up past the mast.

慮.meaning: A <part>tiger</part> stops at a zebra crossing to <part>think</part>. He looks left, looks right, then left again, while the zebras on the stripes wait politely for him. Only when the green man shows does he stroll across, tail high. His mother taught him <kanji>prudence</kanji>.
慮.on: On the far side he orders one small glass of <sound>Rio</sound>ja and sips it very slowly.
慮.kun: Past the crossing he hums along to an <sound>o</sound>boe on the freshly <sound>mown</sound> verge, then shares <sound>pa</sound>sta with a <sound>coo</sound>k, pausing to ponder before every bite.

踊.meaning: Every night the museum locks its ballroom with a heavy <part>padlock</part>. At midnight a marble <part>foot</part> from the statue hall hops over, taps the lock open with its toes and twirls round the empty floor until dawn. The guard never wonders why the lock is warm. The foot loves to <kanji>dance</kanji>.
踊.on: It spins a <sound>yo</sound>-yo on its big toe as it waltzes.
踊.kun: An <sound>o</sound>boe plays from a dusty case, and a <sound>do</sound>lphin statue claps along.

絞.meaning: At the knitting club, two balls of <part>thread</part> <part>mingle</part> under the table, twist round each other and loop about the teapot. They pull tighter and tighter until the pot squeaks and tea squirts out of the spout. The knitters gasp: their yarn is trying to <kanji>strangle</kanji> the teapot.
絞.on: One knitter catches the squirting tea in an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
絞.kun: Another squeezes the soggy wool out over a <sound>shee</sound>p-shaped cushion and a little <sound>bo</sound>nsai.

帳.meaning: A lifeguard has no paper, so he writes the name of every swimmer, every lost sandal and every jellyfish sighting on a very <part>long</part> beach <part>towel</part>. By August the towel trails down the sand, covered in ink. It's his <kanji>notebook</kanji>.
帳.on: When it's full, he starts scratching names onto his <sound>cho</sound>ker necklace.
帳.kun: At sunset he hangs the towel from a <sound>to</sound>tem pole as a curtain, so his <sound>bu</sound>dgie can sleep by the <sound>ree</sound>f.

垂.meaning: In a heatwave, a candle maker hangs his candles on a tall <part>pole</part>, <part>one</part> straight bar above another. By noon the top candle has bent into a soft <part>slash</part>, and the rest bow lower every hour, wicks pointing at the ground. All his candles <kanji>droop</kanji>.
垂.on: Below them, a child's <sound>swee</sound>t melts and bends over its stick.
垂.kun: In her other hand, a <sound>ta</sound>co flops over too.
